### fable-1-1
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/Audience.ts:17
- class: schema   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 19 (LiteralKit for named internal literal domains); AGENTS.md Code Laws ("named LiteralKit internal domains over ad-hoc predicate helpers"); standards/schema-first-development-prompt.md "Derive behavior instead of duplicating truth" (LiteralKit over duplicate literal arrays and literal predicates); D5 (kits land in S4)   evidence: Audience.ts:17 `export type AudienceKind = "human" | "agent" | "ci"`; :45 `const KINDS: ReadonlyArray<AudienceKind> = ["human", "agent", "ci"]` repeats the domain; :100 `KINDS.find((candidate) => candidate === value)` is the hand-rolled membership predicate; :103 `KINDS.join("|")`. The domain is named, exported, and referenced by name (AudienceShape.kind, EnvOverride `Record<AudienceKind, ...>`, Audience.detect). The four beep-law gates do not check law 19 (lint:schema-first is not in the S1 lint set), so the gate did not miss it; it is out of its scope.
- failure: The type, the literal array and the predicate are three independent spellings of one domain: adding a kind to the type does not add it to KINDS or to the override parser, and the compiler does not connect them (KINDS is annotated ReadonlyArray<AudienceKind>, so a missing literal compiles). No schema, no `S.is` guard and no arbitrary exist for the audience kind, which blocks the D10 property floor for AudienceShape consumers.
- fix: In Audience.ts: `export const AudienceKind = LiteralKit(["human", "agent", "ci"]).annotate($I.annoteSchema("AudienceKind", { description: "Who the output is for: a person at a terminal, an AI agent, or a CI job." }));` and `export type AudienceKind = typeof AudienceKind.Type;` (import `LiteralKit` from "@beep/schema", `S` from "effect/Schema"); delete KINDS; at :100 use `if (S.is(AudienceKind)(value)) return { kind: value, source: "override" } satisfies AudienceShape;` and at :103 `AudienceKind.literals.join("|")`. Keep index.ts:11 as `export type { AudienceKind, ... }` so `scratchpad/test/env/entrypoints.test.ts` (which pins the barrel's runtime keys to exactly Audience/CurrentRuntimeEnv/EnvOverride/RuntimeEnv/TerminalEnv) stays byte-identical; if the value is exported from the barrel instead, record it under README Port notes -> Added exports and ledger `exportsAdded`, and adjust entrypoints.test.ts as a `law:19` deviation per section 14.

### fable-1-2
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/RuntimeEnv.ts:53
- class: schema   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 19; standards/schema-first-development-prompt.md "Derive behavior instead of duplicating truth" and "For a non-class schema, export its runtime type from the same identifier"; D5   evidence: RuntimeEnv.ts:33 `export type CiName = "github-actions" | "generic"`; :53 `ci: optionField(Schema.Literals(["github-actions", "generic"]))` spells the literals again inside the class; internal/agentCi.ts:80 `detectCi = (env: Env): O.Option<"github-actions" | "generic">` spells them a third time. The schema field is the only runtime carrier and it does not reference the named type at all.
- failure: The wire schema and the exported CiName type can drift without a compile error on the schema side (Schema.Literals is inferred from its own array, not from CiName); a renamed or added CI name must be edited in three files by hand. There is no `S.is(CiName)` guard or `.literals` for consumers that match CI names, and no single annotated identity for the domain despite the identity step requiring one per schema.
- fix: Define the kit where the domain is decided to avoid a runtime import cycle: in internal/agentCi.ts add `const $I = $ScratchpadId.create("effected/env/internal/agentCi")`, `export const CiName = LiteralKit(["github-actions", "generic"]).annotate($I.annoteSchema("CiName", { description: "github-actions when GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, generic for any other CI signal." }));`, `export type CiName = typeof CiName.Type;`, and type `detectCi` as `O.Option<CiName>`. In RuntimeEnv.ts: `import { CiName } from "./internal/agentCi.ts"; export { CiName };` (replacing the hand-written type at :33, keeping its JSDoc) and `ci: optionField(CiName).annotateKey(...)` at :53. index.ts:15 `export type { CiName, ... }` stays unchanged, so entrypoints.test.ts still passes and parity sees kind `type` (runner/Ledger.schema.ts:264: `both` would also cover it).

### fable-1-3
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/osc8/env.ts:25
- class: effect-idiom   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md "Dual-Arity Inventory Contract" ("A callable shaped `(input, options?)` is excluded because its one-argument form is already complete"); scratchpad/EFFECTED_PORT_GOAL.md operator ruling 2026-10-09 ("lab changes no law, diagnostic or ruling forced ... restore the upstream shape"); EF-18 (standards/effect-first-development.md:465) requires a real data-last form when dual is used   evidence: env.ts:22-32 declares `(value: string | undefined, spec?: TruthySpec): boolean` and `(spec?: TruthySpec): (value: string | undefined) => boolean` and builds it with `dual((args) => args.length >= 1, ...)`. Any one-argument call is therefore routed data-first, so the data-last overload can only be hit by `envIsTruthy()` with no spec. Read-only probe (`bun -e` from scratchpad/): `envIsTruthy("no-color")` -> `true` (typeof boolean); `envIsTruthy()` -> typeof function; `envIsTruthy("0", "no-color")` -> true. Upstream (oracle src/internal/osc8/env.ts:19) is the plain `(value, spec = "default") => boolean`, which is exactly the `(input, options?)` shape the contract excludes from dual, and no tsgo rule at error forces it (missing-pipeable-signature and missed-pipeable-opportunity are both default `off`, docs/rules/*.md).
- failure: The second overload advertises a curried `envIsTruthy(spec)(value)` form that does not exist at runtime: `envIsTruthy("no-color")` is a boolean, not a predicate, so any future caller that writes `A.filter(values, envIsTruthy("no-color"))` type-checks against overload 2 only when it passes zero args and otherwise gets a boolean where a function is expected. The dual is an unforced shape change with a dead overload.
- fix: Restore the upstream signature, keeping the HashSet: `export const envIsTruthy = (value: string | undefined, spec: TruthySpec = "default"): boolean => { if (value === undefined || value === "") return false; if (spec === "no-color") return true; return !HashSet.has(DEFAULT_FALSY, value.toLowerCase()); };` and drop the `dual` import. (If a data-last form is wanted later, it needs `spec` required in the curried overload and `dual(2, ...)`, which is a shape decision, not a port fix.)

### fable-1-4

### fable-1-5
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/RuntimeEnv.ts:55
- class: schema   severity: backlog
- standard: standards/schema-first-development-prompt.md Pattern 1 ("Replace a parallel type ... with one schema") and "export its runtime type from the same identifier"; operator step 4 (identity annotations on schemas)   evidence: RuntimeEnv.ts:55 nests an anonymous `Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String, version: optionField(Schema.String) })` with no identity annotation; RuntimeEnvOverrides.terminal at :88 hand-writes the same shape `{ readonly name: string; readonly version: O.Option<string> }`; internal/osc8/detect.ts:163 writes it a third time structurally. ### fable-1-7
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/EnvOverride.ts:62
- class: effect-idiom   severity: backlog
- standard: standards/effect-first-development.md EF-14 (`Effect.fn("Owner.method")` for public effectful functions; `Effect.fnUntraced` for internal paths); repo convention verified with `rg -o 'Effect\.fn("[^"]+"' packages` (top names: "FileSystem.FileSystem.readFileString", "OntologyFileStore.read", "PromotionGate.evaluate", "User.load")   evidence: Span names are bare: EnvOverride.ts:62 `Effect.fn("readResult")`, :117 `Effect.fn("read")`, TerminalEnv.ts:214 `Effect.fn("colorLevel")`; TerminalEnv.ts:110 `Effect.fn("snapshot")` traces a module-private helper that is only ever called from the two layer constructors. ### fable-1-8
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/colorDepth.ts:57
- class: effect-idiom   severity: backlog
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 21 (tersest equivalent helper form, direct helper refs over trivial lambdas); the `terse-effect` gate passed, so this is reviewer judgment beyond what the checker encodes   evidence: colorDepth.ts:57 defines `const isSet = (value: string | undefined): boolean => value !== undefined && value !== ""` and uses it at :70, yet the same file re-inlines the test at :75 `(env.TMUX ?? "") !== ""`, :94 `(env.TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION === undefined || env.TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION === "")`, :105 and :116. The same predicate is inlined in three spellings across internal/agentCi.ts:11, :55, :62-65 (a block-bodied arrow inside the `if` condition), internal/osc8/wrappers.ts:22-23, internal/osc8/terminals.ts:120, :136, :166, :216, :306, internal/osc8/semver.ts:36 and internal/osc8/detect.ts:74, :108. ### fable-1-9
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/colorDepth.ts:99
- class: effect-idiom   severity: backlog
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 11 (Match over switch) and law 21; installed API: node_modules/effect/dist/Match.d.ts:1910 `Match.option`   evidence: colorDepth.ts:92-101 ends the TERM_PROGRAM matcher with `Match.orElse(() => undefined)` and then branches on `if (programLevel !== undefined) return programLevel;`, re-introducing an `undefined` sentinel for "no arm matched" inside Effect-idiomatic code. The port replaced upstream's `switch` (law 11) but kept the fall-through as a nullable.
- failure: The sentinel conflates "no TERM_PROGRAM arm matched" with a hypothetical arm returning undefined; a reader cannot tell from the type that the arms are total over ColorLevel.
- fix: Finish the matcher with `Match.option` (arms stay `(): ColorLevel => ...`) and branch with `if (O.isSome(programLevel)) return programLevel.value;`.
